summary: Actors package complete: ActorViews replaces the stub. It builds one view set per sim player, rebinds on SessionStarted (attract restarts included) and drives every view from LateUpdate at execution order 150 (after CameraRig 100, before ActorFieldCamera 200), with one try/catch per view, logged once, and no per-frame managed garbage. ThreadView builds a FieldStroke triangle list on layer 31 along a uniform Catmull-Rom display curve sampled every 0.15 u: visible radius 0.17, a 2.2x neck over the first 0.3 u, thinning to 0.74x over the last 0.45 u (inside HeadGrace), tip at RenderPos, MarkDynamic, bounds = trail bbox + 1 u. After a cut it draws [0, s_cut - 0.25] with a pinched taper and [RenderSparkS, L]. After an unchased return with cells the thread lingers as a ghost that dissolves where B1's fill wave arrives (per-vertex amplitude, same rule as TerritoryField). After a chased (saved) return, contract 24 (v1.4) applies: the remaining thread pieces break into small evaporating beads (0.4 s). PearlView: Bead impostor (HeadRadius) plus FieldBlob neck (A 1, 0.8 HeadRadius); squash and stretch along velocity clamped to 0.88..1.15; springy wobble on turns; a 0.15 s exit pop when the 23.3 detach becomes visible; a 0.2 s merge squash exactly on the Return event (only for a Return with cells or after a visible detach); a 4 Hz 1.0..1.08 pulse while the human is chased. RetractionView: a teardrop FieldBlob bulb (r 0.26, stretch 1.32) whose leading edge is at RenderSparkS, with jitter and a flickering glint. It is pulled back and absorbed within 0.03 u of the pearl rim, so it never overlaps the pearl. A droplet chain every 0.45 u (r 0.07-0.12, deterministic, shivering) is one dynamic bead mesh per player; it evaporates on a saved return and fades on a catch. Also implemented: CutFlash (3 blinks over 0.6 s at every on-screen cut), HomeArrow (NearestOwned chevron, 10 Hz query), SparkEdgeIndicator (static IsVisible / ScreenPosition, pulse faster as SparkCatchEta drops), RingView (glossy torus, bob 0.08, slow tilted spin, halo, pop-in, fly to the picker), ChargeRing, RingIndicator, and SplashView (8-12 drops over 0.5 s). Bead.shadergraph and Overlay.shadergraph are thin graphs cloned from ThinUnlitTransparent (VertexColor, UV0, UV1, UV2 into one Custom Function) with fixed-GUID .hlsl files. Both compile 6 passes and ShaderCheck PASSes. Visual loop: 7 builds and DevShot runs into Build/B2, every PNG looked at next to docs/reference_gouttes.png. V2, V3, V4 and V7 hold (docs/waveB/shots/B2).

Overlay vertex layout: UV0.xy = local shape coordinate in [-1,1]^2, UV0.z = world units per local unit; UV1 = (shape id, a, b, c); UV2 = (cos, sin of the local frame, 0, lobes). contract_issues: Contract 24 (v1.4) changes 12.3 for a saved chased return: implemented as written (thread pieces and droplet chain dissolve into small evaporating beads over 0.4 s, pearl merges, no fill). This replaces 12.3's 'droplets absorbed (fade 0.3 s)' for that case. A catch still fades the chain (0.3 s) while the splash plays.

12.3 Beads gives alpha = saturate((1 - |q|) * radiusInPixels). That puts the 50 % edge half a pixel inside the radius. Bead.hlsl adds +0.5 so the antialiased edge is centered on the true radius (still 1 px wide), which keeps the 0.07 u droplets (about 2 px at 540x960) their real size.

V7 vs a near-tie: the bulb's leading edge is exactly at RenderSparkS until it comes within 0.03 u of the pearl rim (gap < HeadRadius + 0.03). It is then pulled back and absorbed over 0.25 u, so it never overlaps the pearl. Only in the last ~0.1 s before a catch, or on a return with Margin < ~0.045 s, does the drawn bulb trail the sim spark. The downstream thread still starts exactly at RenderSparkS, so the drawn gap equals the sim gap.

12.3 does not say what happens to the thread after an unchased return. Removing it instantly left a hole until the 0.35 s fill reached the far side of the loop, and a fixed-time ghost left a raised ridge on the fresh puddle (fA = a + t > 1). ThreadView therefore mirrors B1's fill rule: cell time = Return.Time + FillDuration * d / dMax on the sim render clock. ThreadView.FillDuration duplicates TerritoryField.FillDuration (0.35).

The ring, charge ring, ring indicator and spark edge indicator never appear in the demo (no ring spawns, and the camera keeps the front on screen). Their look was verified only through the -actorgallery overlay (static placements, drawn by the same code paths), not driven by sim events in a player.

Exit neck: the neck's start cap adds field inside the puddle (a + t > 1), which leaves a faint mound where the thread joins the puddle (zoom_exit_neck.png). It is subtle at 540x960. If the polish wave wants it gone: lower the start-cap amplitude (uv0.x) of neck pieces, or have the composite clamp same-color fusion near t = 1.

Size ratio: thread visible radius 0.17 (fixed by 12.3 and TrailHalfWidth) against pearl 0.45 gives about 1:2.6 in width, where the reference shows about 1:4. The pearl still reads clearly as a larger bead (V3).
Exit pop, merge squash, turn wobble, glint flicker, droplet shiver and pulse rates are time effects. Stills show only single frames of them (MidFill shows the merge squash).
